translationRepairs: Zhiyi’s son, born Chixin, succeeded him.
Zhiyi died. His son was called Chixin.
执宜死 explicitly reports Zhiyi's death, and 其子曰赤心 identifies his son as Chixin. The original invents both birth wording and a succession that the sentence does not state.

In the fourth year Keyong led fifty thousand men to save Chenzhou, marched out by Tianjing Pass, and sought a road through Heyang. Ge Zhuang barred the way, so he forded the Yellow River from Hezhong.

In the fourth year Keyong led fifty thousand men to save Chenzhou, marched out by Tianjing Pass, and sought a road through Heyang. Zhuge Shuang barred the way, so he forded the Yellow River from Hezhong.
诸葛 is the compound surname Zhuge and 爽 is Shuang. Ge Zhuang is a false segmentation and reading of the same three characters.

That night, after the drinking ended, Keyong fell asleep in his cups. Quanzhong’s men attacked and set the lodge ablaze. Attendant Guo Jingquan snuffed the lamps, pulled Keyong under the bed, dashed water on his face, and warned him of the ambush.

That night, after the drinking ended, Keyong fell asleep in his cups. Quanzhong’s men attacked and set the lodge ablaze. Attendant Guo Jingzhu snuffed the lamps, pulled Keyong under the bed, dashed water on his face, and warned him of the ambush.
郭景铢 is Guo Jingzhu: 铢 is read zhu, not quan. The replacement corrects the attendant's personal name without changing the event.

In Guangqi 1 (885) Wang Chongrong of Hezhong clashed with the eunuch Tian Lingzi. Chongrong was ordered to Yanzhou and Wang Chuncun of Dingzhou was named military governor of Hezhong; Keyong was told to march troops escorting Chuncun into the circuit.

In Guangqi 1 (885) Wang Chongrong of Hezhong clashed with the eunuch Tian Lingzi. Chongrong was ordered to Yanzhou and Wang Chucun of Dingzhou was named military governor of Hezhong; Keyong was told to march troops escorting Chucun into the circuit.
王处存 is Wang Chucun; 处 is read Chu in this name. Chuncun inserts a nonexistent n and recurs in the following narrative.
Yao was Gong’s brother and had backed his claim.
Yao was Gong’s younger brother and had aided Gong in the struggle.
弟 specifies that Yao was Gong's younger brother, and 助珙以争 says he aided Gong in the struggle. The proposal restores both details.
Keyong camped for a month without moving. Zhaozong sent Princes Jiepi of Yan and Yun of Dan to address him as an elder kinsman and beg him to act.
Keyong camped for more than a month without advancing. Zhaozong sent the Prince of Yan, Jiepi, and the Prince of Dan, Yun, to treat him as an elder brother and plead for urgent aid.
月余 means more than a month. 延王戒丕 and 丹王允 are two separately titled princes, and 兄事克用 means they treated Keyong as an elder brother while urgently appealing for help.
In the fourth month Shi Shuzong came in through Tianjing, Zhang Wenjing through Xinkou, Ge Congzhou through Tumen, Wang Churen through Feihu, and Hou Yan through Yindi.
In the fourth month Shi Shuzong came in through Tianjing, Zhang Wenjing through Xinkou, Ge Congzhou through Tumen, Wang Chuzhi through Feihu, and Hou Yan through Yindi.
王处直 is Wang Chuzhi; 直 is zhi, not ren. The proposed correction matches the Chinese and the supplied pinyin.
Keyong held that Liang had dragged the emperor west by force, that Tianyou was no true Tang era, and refused to use it—he still dated events to Tianfu.
Keyong held that Liang had coerced the emperor into moving the capital, that Tianyou was no true Tang era, and refused to use it—he still dated events to Tianfu.
劫天子以迁都 means coercing the emperor to move the capital. The original adds an incorrect westward direction even though the move described in s0134 was to Luoyang.

In the fourth year Keyong marched fifty thousand men to relieve Chenzhou, came out through Tianjing Pass, and asked passage through Heyang; Ge Zhuang of Heyang refused, so he crossed the Yellow River from Hezhong.

In the fourth year Keyong marched fifty thousand men to relieve Chenzhou, came out through Tianjing Pass, and asked passage through Heyang; Zhuge Shuang refused, so he crossed the Yellow River from Hezhong.
The literal field repeated the false segmentation Ge Zhuang for 诸葛爽 and is corrected in parallel with the reviewed idiomatic field.

At night, when the wine was finished, Keyong lay drunk. Assassins sprang up, fire broke out, and his attendant Guo Jingquan extinguished the lamps, hid Keyong under the bed, splashed water on his face, and told him of the danger.

At night, when the wine was finished, Keyong lay drunk. Assassins sprang up, fire broke out, and his attendant Guo Jingzhu extinguished the lamps, hid Keyong under the bed, splashed water on his face, and told him of the danger.
The literal field repeated the misreading Jingquan for 景铢 and is corrected to Jingzhu in parallel with the reviewed idiomatic field.

In the first year of Guangqi, Wang Chongrong of Hezhong quarreled with the eunuch Tian Lingzi; Chongrong was transferred to Yanzhou and Wang Chuncun of Dingzhou was made military governor of Hezhong. An edict ordered Keyong to escort Chuncun to his post with troops.

In the first year of Guangqi, Wang Chongrong of Hezhong quarreled with the eunuch Tian Lingzi; Chongrong was transferred to Yanzhou and Wang Chucun of Dingzhou was made military governor of Hezhong. An edict ordered Keyong to escort Chucun to his post with troops.
The literal field repeated the Chuncun misspelling of 王处存 and is corrected throughout the sentence.
Chongrong sent a man to deceive Keyong, saying, “The Son of Heaven has ordered Chongrong that when Keyong arrives, he and Chuncun are jointly to execute him.”
Chongrong sent a man to deceive Keyong, saying, “The Son of Heaven has ordered Chongrong that when Keyong arrives, he and Chucun are jointly to execute him.”
This following sentence refers to the same Wang Chucun and carried the same misspelled given name in the literal field.
Chongrong sent an agent to trick Keyong: “The emperor has instructed me that once you arrive, Chuncun and I are to kill you together.”
Chongrong sent an agent to trick Keyong: “The emperor has instructed me that once you arrive, Chucun and I are to kill you together.”
This following sentence refers to the same Wang Chucun and carried the same misspelled given name in the idiomatic field.
In the second month he joined Wang Chuncun in attacking Rong; they fought at Xincheng and were defeated by Rong.
In the second month he joined Wang Chucun in attacking Rong; they fought at Xincheng and were defeated by Rong.
The later reference is again to 王处存, so the literal field must use the same corrected name Wang Chucun.
In the second month he allied with Wang Chuncun against Rong, fought at Xincheng, and lost.
In the second month he allied with Wang Chucun against Rong, fought at Xincheng, and lost.
The later reference is again to 王处存, so the idiomatic field must use the same corrected name Wang Chucun.
Keyong’s army halted for more than a month without advancing; Zhaozong sent the Prince of Yan Jiepi and the Prince of Dan Yun to treat Keyong as elder brothers and plead for urgent aid.
Keyong’s army halted for more than a month without advancing; Zhaozong sent Jiepi, Prince of Yan, and Yun, Prince of Dan, to treat Keyong as an elder brother and plead for urgent aid.
The literal field contained the same ambiguous title attachment and an ungrammatical plural in 兄事克用; the paired correction identifies both princes clearly.
In the fourth month Shi Shuzong entered Tianjing, Zhang Wenjing entered Xinkou, Ge Congzhou entered Tumen, Wang Churen entered Feihu, and Hou Yan entered Yindi.
In the fourth month Shi Shuzong entered Tianjing, Zhang Wenjing entered Xinkou, Ge Congzhou entered Tumen, Wang Chuzhi entered Feihu, and Hou Yan entered Yindi.
The literal field repeated the misreading Churen for 处直 and is corrected to Chuzhi in parallel with the reviewed idiomatic field.
